fact: The RBI was set up on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and was nationalised in 1949.
The Monetary Policy Committee has 6 members (3 from RBI, 3 named by the government) and was created by a 2016 amendment to the RBI Act, 1934.
SEBI was set up in 1988 and got legal (statutory) powers under the SEBI Act, 1992.
GST came in on 1 July 2017 through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016; the GST Council is under Article 279A.
The Finance Commission is set up by the President every five years under Article 280.
The Union Budget is called the 'Annual Financial Statement' in Article 112 of the Constitution.
A Money Bill is defined in Article 110 and can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act was passed in 2003 to control the government's deficit.
The Election Commission of India works under Article 324 and was set up on 25 January 1950 (now National Voters' Day).
President's Rule in a state is imposed under Article 356 of the Constitution.
Article 153 says each state shall have a Governor, appointed by the President (Article 155).
The Supreme Court is set up under Article 124; Article 32 lets citizens go directly to it to protect Fundamental Rights.
Article 226 gives High Courts power to issue writs, which is wider than the Supreme Court's power under Article 32.
The anti-defection law is in the Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985.
Panchayati Raj got constitutional status through the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 (Part IX of the Constitution).
Urban local bodies got constitutional status through the 74th Amendment Act, 1992 (Part IXA).
The Comptroller and Auditor General is appointed under Article 148.
The UPSC is set up under Article 315 of the Constitution.
Article 370 was made ineffective on 5 August 2019, and J&K was split into two Union Territories.
Parliament can form new states or change state borders under Article 3 of the Constitution.
National Emergency is under Article 352, President's Rule under Article 356 and Financial Emergency under Article 360.
The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House under Article 83; one-third of its members retire every two years.
The Vice-President (Article 63) is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015; the Prime Minister is its Chairperson.
ISRO was founded on 15 August 1969; its headquarters is in Bengaluru.
Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole on 23 August 2023, now marked as National Space Day.
Aditya-L1, India's first solar mission, was launched on 2 September 2023 to the Lagrange point L1.
Gaganyaan is India's human spaceflight programme run by ISRO.
DRDO was formed in 1958 by merging defence science bodies; it works under the Ministry of Defence.
General Bipin Rawat became India's first Chief of Defence Staff on 1 January 2020.
INS Vikrant, India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, was commissioned on 2 September 2022.
BrahMos is an India-Russia joint venture; the name joins the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.
The Agnipath scheme for short-term recruitment of soldiers (Agniveers) was announced in June 2022.
Navy Day is on 4 December, marking Operation Trident against Karachi in the 1971 war.
The Indian Air Force was formed on 8 October 1932; Air Force Day is on 8 October.
Army Day is on 15 January, when General K.M. Cariappa took over as the first Indian Commander-in-Chief in 1949.
The Indian Coast Guard was set up in 1977 and works under the Ministry of Defence.
The United Nations was founded on 24 October 1945 (UN Day); it has 193 member states.
The UN Security Council has 15 members: 5 permanent with veto power (US, UK, France, Russia, China) and 10 elected for two years.
NATO was founded on 4 April 1949 by the Washington Treaty; Article 5 says an attack on one member is an attack on all.
The Quad (India, US, Japan, Australia) began in 2007 and was revived in 2017.
BRIC held its first summit in 2009; South Africa joined in 2010, and the group added Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and UAE in 2024 and Indonesia in 2025.
The SCO was formed in 2001 in Shanghai; India and Pakistan became full members in 2017.
SAARC was formed on 8 December 1985 in Dhaka; its secretariat is in Kathmandu.
BIMSTEC was formed by the Bangkok Declaration of 1997; its secretariat is in Dhaka.
ASEAN was formed on 8 August 1967 in Bangkok; India's 'Act East Policy' focuses on it.
The G20 was formed in 1999; under India's presidency in 2023 the African Union became a permanent member.
The IMF and World Bank were created at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944.
The WTO started on 1 January 1995 in Geneva, replacing GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 1947).
OPEC was formed in 1960 in Baghdad; its headquarters is in Vienna.
The ICJ sits in The Hague and has 15 judges elected for nine years.
The ICC was created by the Rome Statute (1998); India is not a member.
The IAEA was set up in 1957 in Vienna; India has not signed the NPT (1968).
Under UNCLOS (UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982) a country's EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles from its coast.
Article 51 of the UN Charter allows a country to defend itself if attacked.
The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960 with World Bank help; India put it 'in abeyance' in April 2025 after the Pahalgam attack.
The Simla Agreement (1972) between India and Pakistan turned the ceasefire line in J&K into the Line of Control.
The India-China border (LAC) is about 3,488 km long; the 1954 Panchsheel Agreement set five principles of peaceful co-existence.
The India-Bangladesh border (about 4,096 km) is India's longest land border; the Land Boundary Agreement was put into effect in 2015.
India and Nepal signed the Treaty of Peace and Friendship in 1950, allowing open borders.
The India-Bhutan Friendship Treaty of 1949 was revised in 2007.
India gave Katchatheevu island to Sri Lanka under a 1974 agreement.
In 1988 India's Operation Cactus stopped a coup attempt in the Maldives.
India and Myanmar share a land border of about 1,643 km touching four north-eastern states.
The Taliban took back power in Afghanistan on 15 August 2021 after US forces left.
The Bab-el-Mandeb strait links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden; much India-Europe trade passes through it.
The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf to the Arabian Sea; a large share of world oil exports passes through it.
Russia annexed Crimea in March 2014; the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began on 24 February 2022.
Gaza borders Israel and Egypt; the current war began with the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.
Nobel Prizes were first given in 1901 as per Alfred Nobel's will; the Economics prize was added in 1968.
Patents in India are governed by the Patents Act, 1970.
India's GDP data is released by the National Statistics Office (NSO) under MoSPI.
Under the inflation-targeting framework, the RBI aims to keep CPI inflation at 4% with a band of 2% to 6%.
UPI was launched in 2016 by NPCI (set up in 2008 by RBI and the Indian Banks' Association).
Elections to Parliament and state assemblies are held under the Representation of the People Acts of 1950 and 1951.
UNESCO's World Heritage list comes from the World Heritage Convention of 1972.
The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to keep warming well below 2 degrees C, trying for 1.5 degrees C.
The modern Olympics began in Athens in 1896; India will bid to host the 2036 Games.
Article 1 of the Constitution says: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.'
The UN has six main organs: General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ and the Secretariat.
Seventh Schedule: List II (State List) gives states power over police, public order, health and agriculture.
The Supreme Commander of India's armed forces is the President (Article 53).
A party is recognised as a 'national party' by the Election Commission under the Symbols Order, 1968.
The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 gives the RBI power to license and control banks.
India's financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March.
India shares land borders with seven countries: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Afghanistan.
National Science Day (28 February) marks C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect in 1928.
Panchsheel (1954) gave five principles of peaceful co-existence, including respect for each other's sovereignty.
The Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, was started in 1954.
The four Geneva Conventions of 1949 set the rules for treating wounded soldiers, prisoners of war and civilians.
